output.summary: KEP-2505 proposes a kubeadm operator that applies the operator pattern to kubeadm workflows, giving declarative control over operations such as kubeadm upgrade, certificate renewal, certificate authority rotation, and cluster configuration changes across existing nodes. Its status is provisional (since 2021-02-17).
output.rationale: kubeadm runs only on the local machine, so multi-node workflows like upgrades must be run and ordered by hand, which is error-prone. The KEP applies the operator pattern to automate and orchestrate these tasks across nodes. The current iteration is limited to getting approval on the Summary and Motivation and defining operation semantics, workflow management, user interaction, and deployment.

alternatives.option: Do not implement the kubeadm operator; let users automate kubeadm workflows and cross-node orchestration with other tools.
alternatives.why_not: The sources list this only as an alternative and do not record why it was not chosen.

alternatives.option: Keep kubeadm raw workflows as the only path.
alternatives.why_not: The KEP states the operator is not meant to replace them: "The user will always be able to run kubeadm workflows in isolation in manual fashion." Manual execution is the problem the KEP targets, so this is a constraint rather than a rejected option.

evidence.quote: Kubeadm binary can execute operations only on the machine where it is running e.g. it is not possible to execute operations on other nodes, to copy files across nodes, etc.
The manual approach can be considered a blocker for implementing more complex workflows such as rotating certificate authorities
This KEP aims to address such problems by applying the operator pattern to kubeadm workflows.
The user will always be able to run kubeadm workflows in isolation in manual fashion.
